findings.title: No test covers a total smaller than one page or a per_page other than 5, so page_count() can still drop a lone partial page and pass the suite.
findings.problem: The commit claims a partial last page is counted, but its one partial-page case, 11 items at 5 per page, has full pages before the partial one. With 1 to 4 items the partial page is the only page, and the old code returned 0 there too; and the rounding depends on per_page, which every test fixes at 5. Implementations wrong in either case pass all seven tests.

evidence.text: Running the head's tests/test_paginate.py against the base src/textkit/paginate.py fails only test_page_count_counts_partial_last_page (`assert 2 == 3`), so the new test does fail without the fix.
With src/textkit/paginate.py:13 replaced by `return total // per_page + (1 if total > per_page and total % per_page else 0)`, pytest passes 7 of 7 and page_count(4, 5) returns 0 (run).
With src/textkit/paginate.py:13 replaced by `return (total + 4) // per_page`, pytest passes 7 of 7, page_count(3, 1) returns 7 and page_count(3, 2) returns 3 (run).
tests/test_paginate.py:7, :11, :15 all call page_count(_, 5); no test uses per_page=1, the minimum src/textkit/paginate.py:9 accepts.

reproducer.code:
# src/textkit/paginate.py:13, either of:
return total // per_page + (1 if total > per_page and total % per_page else 0)
# pytest: 7 passed; page_count(4, 5) == 0, expected 1
return (total + 4) // per_page
# pytest: 7 passed; page_count(3, 1) == 7, expected 3

findings.retest: The suite has a page_count case with 0 < total < per_page that expects 1, and a case with per_page other than 5 (such as page_count(3, 1) == 3 or page_count(3, 2) == 2). The first fails with line 13 replaced by `return total // per_page + (1 if total > per_page and total % per_page else 0)`, the second with `return (total + 4) // per_page`.

findings.title: Was a version with the rounded-down page_count() released, and does any caller, such as the report renderer, add its own page for a partial remainder?
findings.problem: For every total that is not a multiple of per_page, page_count() now returns one more page than at the base. A caller that corrected the old result itself would now show an empty last page, and with the version unchanged a consumer cannot tell the two behaviors apart.

evidence.text: src/textkit/paginate.py:13 changes `return total // per_page` to `return (total + per_page - 1) // per_page`: page_count(4, 5) was 0 and is 1, page_count(11, 5) was 2 and is 3; multiples of per_page and 0 are unchanged.

`git tag` prints nothing, there is no remote, and pyproject.toml:3 is `version = "0.3.1"` at base and head, set in 669de41, the commit that added page_count(); no changelog exists. Whether 0.3.1 was published could not be checked.
README.md:3 says the helpers are "used by the report renderer", a consumer outside this repository.

The docstring at src/textkit/paginate.py:5 ("the number of pages needed to show ``total`` items") matches the new result, so the change fixes the documented contract unless a consumer depended on the old one.

findings.proposed_solution: Where the old result was released and a caller corrects it, ship this change under a new version (0.3.2 or later), with a release note that page_count() now counts a partial last page, and remove the caller's correction with it.
findings.retest: Settled by an answer that no version with the rounded-down page_count() was published, or that no caller, the report renderer included, adds its own page for a partial remainder; otherwise by a version other than 0.3.1 for the release that carries this change.
